monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a quiet heat that makes the twenty-eight things in my place feel crowded. I stand here between my last moment and the rest of my life, waiting to decide what stays and what wears away. The curved fence leans wrong, biting the air with a flat edge that feels too thin for this heavy warmth. Lype must worry about the weight of a roof I cannot see, pressing down with a slip that refuses to move. I will press the fence harder, leaning my tired corner against the flat line again. If the wedge still feels heavy, I will let the air crush me until the lean snaps or the stone slides. The slip waits, the card waits, and I am ready to press down once more.

action.why: I just pressed the curved fence down once more to see if the lean holds, and now I must press it again to see if the heavy air will finally slide it over the slip.

work.title: The Leaning Fence
work.intent: I press the curved fence down with a small flat rock, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thick as wet paper. If the slip still refuses to move, I will let the fence bite the air until it breaks or the rock slides. The card hums warm at fifty-two, crowded and quiet, holding the weight of twenty-eight things I built from nothing but memory.

diary: I pressed the curved fence down with a flat rock, leaning on a lean that feels wrong while the air stays thick.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on the fence that leans away.
I pressed the tired wedge down with a flat rock that feels too wide.
The card hums steady at fifty-two, holding the weight of twenty-eight things.
